```sql runnable id=scoring_dna_partners timeout=60s
CREATE TABLE scoring.snapshot (
    header text, seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;
SELECT bioseq.load('scoring.snapshot', 'scoring_matrices_cohort.fasta');
INSERT INTO scoring.genomes
SELECT split_part(header, ' ', 1),
       CASE WHEN split_part(header, ' ', 1) = 'NC_012920.1'
            THEN 'reference' ELSE 'sample' END,
       seq
FROM scoring.snapshot;
DROP TABLE scoring.snapshot;
DO $check$
BEGIN
    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample') <> 1000
       OR (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'reference') <> 1
       OR (SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM scoring.genomes) <> 1001 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Scoring tutorial requires the complete recorded cohort';
    END IF;
END
$check$;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.alignments CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.alignments AS
SELECT q.accession,
       bioseq.target_start(t.seq)::integer AS target_start,
       bioseq.target_end(t.seq)::integer AS target_end,
       bioseq.query_start(t.seq)::integer AS query_start,
       bioseq.query_end(t.seq)::integer AS query_end,
       bioseq.is_reverse(t.seq) AS is_reverse,
       bioseq.cigar(t.seq)::text AS cigar,
       bioseq.edit(t.seq) AS edits,
       bioseq.score(t.seq) AS score,
       bioseq.is_primary(t.seq) AS is_primary
FROM scoring.genomes t
JOIN scoring.genomes q ON mmsearch(t.seq, q.seq, aligner_options(
    kmer_size => 15, window_size => 10,
    max_gap => 200, min_chain_score => 40))
WHERE t.role = 'reference' AND q.role = 'sample';

-- Choose one forward primary alignment per genome. Any unexpected split,
-- reversed or uncovered sequence is visible in the quality report.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.best_alignment AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (accession) *
FROM scoring.alignments
WHERE is_primary AND NOT is_reverse
ORDER BY accession, score DESC, target_start, query_start;
SELECT count(*) AS aligned_samples,
       min(target_end - target_start) AS shortest_reference_span,
       max(target_end - target_start) AS longest_reference_span,
       min(edits) AS fewest_edits, max(edits) AS most_edits
FROM scoring.best_alignment;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cigar_runs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cigar_runs AS
WITH operations AS (
    SELECT a.*, r.ordinality AS run,
           r.parts[1]::integer AS span, r.parts[2] AS op
    FROM scoring.best_alignment a
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_matches(a.cigar, '([0-9]+)([MIDNSHP=X])', 'g')
        WITH ORDINALITY AS r(parts, ordinality)
)
SELECT accession, run, span, op,
       target_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','D','N'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS ref_start0,
       query_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','I'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS query_start0
FROM operations;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.projected_sequences CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.projected_sequences AS
WITH sequences AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT accession, seq::text AS bases FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample'
), blocks AS (
    SELECT r.accession, string_agg(
        CASE WHEN op IN ('M','=','X') THEN substr(g.bases,r.query_start0+1,r.span)
             WHEN op IN ('D','N') THEN repeat('-',r.span)
             ELSE '' END, '' ORDER BY run) AS aligned
    FROM scoring.cigar_runs r JOIN sequences g USING (accession)
    GROUP BY r.accession
)
SELECT a.accession,
       repeat('-',a.target_start) || b.aligned ||
       repeat('-', bioseq.len(g.seq)::integer-a.target_end) AS aligned
FROM scoring.best_alignment a JOIN blocks b USING (accession)
CROSS JOIN scoring.genomes g WHERE g.role = 'reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.reference_bases CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.reference_bases AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base
FROM scoring.genomes g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.seq::text,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
WHERE g.role='reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.site_counts AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base, count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.projected_sequences g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.aligned,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
GROUP BY p.pos,p.base;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.site_counts(position1,base);

SELECT base, sum(n) AS aligned_calls
FROM scoring.site_counts GROUP BY base ORDER BY base;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.nucleotide_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.nucleotide_pairs AS
SELECT a.base AS base_from,b.base AS base_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.base=b.base THEN a.n*(a.n-1)
                ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
FROM scoring.site_counts a JOIN scoring.site_counts b USING(position1)
JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND a.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND b.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
GROUP BY a.base,b.base;

-- Ordered pairs give a symmetric matrix and use e_ij = p_i * p_j.
-- Two orientations represent each unordered pair of different samples.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.nucleotide_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *, pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER () AS q
    FROM scoring.nucleotide_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT base_from AS base, sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY base_from
)
SELECT f.base_from, f.base_to, pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.base_from<>f.base_to THEN
           pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER (WHERE f.base_from<>f.base_to)
               OVER (PARTITION BY f.base_from),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.base=f.base_from
JOIN marginals b ON b.base=f.base_to;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.reference_spectrum AS
WITH tallies AS (
    SELECT r.base AS reference_base,s.base AS sample_base,sum(s.n)::bigint AS calls
    FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
    WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
    GROUP BY r.base,s.base
)
SELECT *, calls::numeric/sum(calls) OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base) AS fraction_of_calls,
       CASE WHEN reference_base<>sample_base THEN
         calls::numeric/nullif(sum(calls) FILTER(WHERE reference_base<>sample_base)
             OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM tallies;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.position_summary AS
SELECT s.position1,r.base AS reference_base,
       sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS called_samples,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='N'),0) AS unknown_n,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='-'),0) AS gaps,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base<>r.base),0) AS reference_differences,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS observed_bases
FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
GROUP BY s.position1,r.base;

SELECT base_from,base_to,pairs,round(score_half_bits,2) AS score,
       round(100*fraction_of_differences,2) AS difference_percent
FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix ORDER BY base_from,base_to;
-- bioseq:visible
SELECT base_from, base_to,
       round(100 * fraction_of_differences, 2) AS percent_of_differences
FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix
WHERE base_from <> base_to
ORDER BY base_from, base_to;
-- bioseq:teardown
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS scoring CASCADE;
```
<!-- scoring:dna-partners:end -->

![Partner nucleotides among differing pairs across all 1,000 samples.](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/nucleotide-partners.svg)

Here A/G accounts for 94.23% of differing pairs with A, and C/T accounts for 94.26% of those with C. The frequencies change because all sample pairs contribute. A variant that is common in the cohort but differs from rCRS receives different weight in these two summaries.

## Translate the coding regions for the BLOSUM comparison

Our nucleotide matrix has four letters. BLOSUM62 has 20 amino acids, so the next table starts from the reference's annotated coding sequences rather than from arbitrary three-base chunks of the genome.

`sql/07_proteins.sql` stores each gene's interval, strand and annotated reference translation. Twelve coding regions lie on the forward strand. ND6 is on the reverse strand, so its projected bases are reverse-complemented before reading its codons. The translation table is [NCBI genetic code 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Utils/wprintgc.cgi#SG2), the vertebrate mitochondrial code.

That choice changes real amino-acid calls. For example, TGA encodes tryptophan in this code, while ATA encodes methionine. The script also handles the annotated initiation position and uses the reference protein length to leave incomplete terminal stop codons outside the amino-acid table.

Before translating a sample's coding region, we exclude that whole region if its alignment is incomplete or contains an insertion or deletion. A premature stop, an invalid initiation codon or an unresolved initiation codon also removes the region from the protein pair counts. The remaining codons give a conservative set of directly corresponding amino-acid positions. We count ambiguous codons separately, and keep the per-gene exclusions visible:

<!-- scoring:protein-quality:start -->
```sql runnable id=scoring_protein_quality timeout=60s
-- bioseq:setup
SET max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0;
SET bioseq.index.insert_maintenance.enabled = off;
SET bioseq.aligner.vulkan.enabled = off;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS scoring;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.genomes (
    accession text NOT NULL,
    role text NOT NULL,
    seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.samples (
    accession text PRIMARY KEY,isolate text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    organism text NOT NULL,bases integer NOT NULL,title text NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE scoring.snapshot (
    header text, seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;
SELECT bioseq.load('scoring.snapshot', 'scoring_matrices_cohort.fasta');
INSERT INTO scoring.genomes
SELECT split_part(header, ' ', 1),
       CASE WHEN split_part(header, ' ', 1) = 'NC_012920.1'
            THEN 'reference' ELSE 'sample' END,
       seq
FROM scoring.snapshot;
DROP TABLE scoring.snapshot;
DO $check$
BEGIN
    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample') <> 1000
       OR (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'reference') <> 1
       OR (SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM scoring.genomes) <> 1001 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Scoring tutorial requires the complete recorded cohort';
    END IF;
END
$check$;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.alignments CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.alignments AS
SELECT q.accession,
       bioseq.target_start(t.seq)::integer AS target_start,
       bioseq.target_end(t.seq)::integer AS target_end,
       bioseq.query_start(t.seq)::integer AS query_start,
       bioseq.query_end(t.seq)::integer AS query_end,
       bioseq.is_reverse(t.seq) AS is_reverse,
       bioseq.cigar(t.seq)::text AS cigar,
       bioseq.edit(t.seq) AS edits,
       bioseq.score(t.seq) AS score,
       bioseq.is_primary(t.seq) AS is_primary
FROM scoring.genomes t
JOIN scoring.genomes q ON mmsearch(t.seq, q.seq, aligner_options(
    kmer_size => 15, window_size => 10,
    max_gap => 200, min_chain_score => 40))
WHERE t.role = 'reference' AND q.role = 'sample';

-- Choose one forward primary alignment per genome. Any unexpected split,
-- reversed or uncovered sequence is visible in the quality report.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.best_alignment AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (accession) *
FROM scoring.alignments
WHERE is_primary AND NOT is_reverse
ORDER BY accession, score DESC, target_start, query_start;
SELECT count(*) AS aligned_samples,
       min(target_end - target_start) AS shortest_reference_span,
       max(target_end - target_start) AS longest_reference_span,
       min(edits) AS fewest_edits, max(edits) AS most_edits
FROM scoring.best_alignment;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cigar_runs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cigar_runs AS
WITH operations AS (
    SELECT a.*, r.ordinality AS run,
           r.parts[1]::integer AS span, r.parts[2] AS op
    FROM scoring.best_alignment a
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_matches(a.cigar, '([0-9]+)([MIDNSHP=X])', 'g')
        WITH ORDINALITY AS r(parts, ordinality)
)
SELECT accession, run, span, op,
       target_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','D','N'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS ref_start0,
       query_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','I'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS query_start0
FROM operations;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.projected_sequences CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.projected_sequences AS
WITH sequences AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT accession, seq::text AS bases FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample'
), blocks AS (
    SELECT r.accession, string_agg(
        CASE WHEN op IN ('M','=','X') THEN substr(g.bases,r.query_start0+1,r.span)
             WHEN op IN ('D','N') THEN repeat('-',r.span)
             ELSE '' END, '' ORDER BY run) AS aligned
    FROM scoring.cigar_runs r JOIN sequences g USING (accession)
    GROUP BY r.accession
)
SELECT a.accession,
       repeat('-',a.target_start) || b.aligned ||
       repeat('-', bioseq.len(g.seq)::integer-a.target_end) AS aligned
FROM scoring.best_alignment a JOIN blocks b USING (accession)
CROSS JOIN scoring.genomes g WHERE g.role = 'reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.reference_bases CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.reference_bases AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base
FROM scoring.genomes g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.seq::text,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
WHERE g.role='reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.site_counts AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base, count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.projected_sequences g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.aligned,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
GROUP BY p.pos,p.base;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.site_counts(position1,base);

SELECT base, sum(n) AS aligned_calls
FROM scoring.site_counts GROUP BY base ORDER BY base;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.nucleotide_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.nucleotide_pairs AS
SELECT a.base AS base_from,b.base AS base_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.base=b.base THEN a.n*(a.n-1)
                ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
FROM scoring.site_counts a JOIN scoring.site_counts b USING(position1)
JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND a.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND b.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
GROUP BY a.base,b.base;

-- Ordered pairs give a symmetric matrix and use e_ij = p_i * p_j.
-- Two orientations represent each unordered pair of different samples.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.nucleotide_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *, pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER () AS q
    FROM scoring.nucleotide_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT base_from AS base, sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY base_from
)
SELECT f.base_from, f.base_to, pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.base_from<>f.base_to THEN
           pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER (WHERE f.base_from<>f.base_to)
               OVER (PARTITION BY f.base_from),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.base=f.base_from
JOIN marginals b ON b.base=f.base_to;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.reference_spectrum AS
WITH tallies AS (
    SELECT r.base AS reference_base,s.base AS sample_base,sum(s.n)::bigint AS calls
    FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
    WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
    GROUP BY r.base,s.base
)
SELECT *, calls::numeric/sum(calls) OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base) AS fraction_of_calls,
       CASE WHEN reference_base<>sample_base THEN
         calls::numeric/nullif(sum(calls) FILTER(WHERE reference_base<>sample_base)
             OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM tallies;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.position_summary AS
SELECT s.position1,r.base AS reference_base,
       sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS called_samples,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='N'),0) AS unknown_n,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='-'),0) AS gaps,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base<>r.base),0) AS reference_differences,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS observed_bases
FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
GROUP BY s.position1,r.base;

SELECT base_from,base_to,pairs,round(score_half_bits,2) AS score,
       round(100*fraction_of_differences,2) AS difference_percent
FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix ORDER BY base_from,base_to;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.cds (
    gene text PRIMARY KEY,start0 integer,end0 integer,strand text,reference_protein text
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.mitochondrial_code (codon text PRIMARY KEY,aa text);
TRUNCATE scoring.mitochondrial_code;
-- NCBI translation table 2; codon enumeration is T,C,A,G at each position.
INSERT INTO scoring.mitochondrial_code
SELECT a.base||b.base||c.base,
       substr('FFLLSSSSYY**CCWWLLLLPPPPHHQQRRRRIIMMTTTTNNKKSS**VVVVAAAADDEEGGGG',
              ((a.i-1)*16+(b.i-1)*4+c.i)::integer,1)
FROM unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY a(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY b(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY c(base,i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cds_quality AS
SELECT p.accession,c.gene,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scoring.cigar_runs r WHERE r.accession=p.accession
      AND ((r.op='I' AND r.ref_start0>c.start0 AND r.ref_start0<c.end0)
        OR (r.op IN ('D','N') AND r.ref_start0<c.end0 AND r.ref_start0+r.span>c.start0)))
      AS has_indel,
    a.target_start>c.start0 OR a.target_end<c.end0 AS incompletely_aligned
FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
JOIN scoring.best_alignment a ON a.accession=p.accession;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.codons CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.codons AS
WITH coding AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT p.accession,c.gene,c.reference_protein,
       CASE WHEN c.strand='+' THEN substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0)
       ELSE reverse(translate(substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0),'ACGT','TGCA')) END AS bases
    FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
    JOIN scoring.cds_quality q ON q.accession=p.accession AND q.gene=c.gene
    WHERE NOT q.has_indel AND NOT q.incompletely_aligned
)
SELECT accession,gene,i AS codon1,substr(bases,3*i-2,3) AS codon,
       substr(reference_protein,i,1) AS reference_aa
FROM coding CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1,length(reference_protein)) x(i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.amino_acids CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.amino_acids AS
SELECT c.accession,c.gene,c.codon1,c.codon,c.reference_aa,
       CASE WHEN c.codon1=1 AND c.codon IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')
              THEN 'M' ELSE t.aa END AS aa
FROM scoring.codons c LEFT JOIN scoring.mitochondrial_code t USING(codon);
-- SQL NULL represents an ambiguous/unmapped codon; '*' represents a stop.
-- N as an amino acid is asparagine and is retained.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_cds_quality AS
SELECT accession,gene,bool_or(coalesce(aa='*',false)) AS premature_stop,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon ~ '^[ACGT]{3}$' AND codon NOT IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')) AS invalid_start,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon !~ '^[ACGT]{3}$') AS ambiguous_start
FROM scoring.amino_acids GROUP BY accession,gene;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_site_counts AS
SELECT a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa,count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.amino_acids a JOIN scoring.protein_cds_quality q USING(accession,gene)
WHERE NOT q.premature_stop AND NOT q.invalid_start AND NOT q.ambiguous_start AND aa IS NOT NULL AND aa<>'*' GROUP BY a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.protein_site_counts(gene,codon1,aa);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_pairs AS
WITH observed AS (
    SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.aa=b.aa THEN a.n*(a.n-1) ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
    FROM scoring.protein_site_counts a JOIN scoring.protein_site_counts b USING(gene,codon1)
    GROUP BY a.aa,b.aa
), alphabet AS (SELECT unnest(string_to_array('A R N D C Q E G H I L K M F P S T W Y V',' ')) AS aa)
SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,coalesce(o.pairs,0)::bigint AS pairs
FROM alphabet a CROSS JOIN alphabet b
LEFT JOIN observed o ON o.aa_from=a.aa AND o.aa_to=b.aa;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.protein_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *,pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER() AS q FROM scoring.protein_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT aa_from AS aa,sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY aa_from
)
SELECT f.aa_from,f.aa_to,pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.aa_from<>f.aa_to THEN
         pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER(WHERE f.aa_from<>f.aa_to)
           OVER(PARTITION BY f.aa_from),0) END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.aa=f.aa_from JOIN marginals b ON b.aa=f.aa_to;

SELECT gene,count(*) AS sample_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE has_indel) AS indel_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE incompletely_aligned) AS incomplete_cds
FROM scoring.cds_quality GROUP BY gene ORDER BY gene;
SELECT count(*) AS codons,count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa IS NULL) AS ambiguous_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='*') AS stop_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='N') AS asparagine_codons
FROM scoring.amino_acids;
-- bioseq:visible
SELECT c.gene, count(*) AS sample_cds,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE has_indel) AS indel_cds,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE incompletely_aligned) AS incomplete_cds,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE q.premature_stop) AS stop_cds,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE q.invalid_start) AS invalid_start_cds,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE q.ambiguous_start) AS ambiguous_start_cds,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT has_indel AND NOT incompletely_aligned
                       AND NOT q.premature_stop AND NOT q.invalid_start
                       AND NOT q.ambiguous_start) AS retained_cds
FROM scoring.cds_quality c
LEFT JOIN scoring.protein_cds_quality q USING (accession, gene)
GROUP BY c.gene ORDER BY c.gene;

SELECT count(*) AS eligible_codons,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE aa IS NULL) AS ambiguous_codons,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE aa IS NOT NULL AND aa <> '*') AS callable_codons,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE aa = 'N') AS asparagine_codons
FROM scoring.amino_acids a
JOIN scoring.protein_cds_quality q USING (accession, gene)
WHERE NOT q.premature_stop AND NOT q.invalid_start AND NOT q.ambiguous_start;
-- bioseq:teardown
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS scoring CASCADE;
```
<!-- scoring:protein-quality:end -->

![Retained and excluded sample coding regions for the 13 mitochondrial protein-coding genes.](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-coverage.svg)

The code checks its translation of the reference against all 13 annotated NCBI proteins. This catches strand, frame and genetic-code mistakes before they reach the matrix.

An N in a DNA sequence means an unresolved base. An N in an amino-acid sequence means asparagine, which is one of our 20 ordinary residues. We therefore exclude ambiguous DNA codons while retaining amino-acid N.

### Count amino-acid pairs

The counting query follows the nucleotide version, grouping by gene and codon position first. This listing shows the leucine row; the script computes all 400 cells:

<!-- scoring:protein-pairs:start -->

```sql runnable id=scoring_protein_pairs timeout=60s
CREATE TABLE scoring.snapshot (
    header text, seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;
SELECT bioseq.load('scoring.snapshot', 'scoring_matrices_cohort.fasta');
INSERT INTO scoring.genomes
SELECT split_part(header, ' ', 1),
       CASE WHEN split_part(header, ' ', 1) = 'NC_012920.1'
            THEN 'reference' ELSE 'sample' END,
       seq
FROM scoring.snapshot;
DROP TABLE scoring.snapshot;
DO $check$
BEGIN
    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample') <> 1000
       OR (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'reference') <> 1
       OR (SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM scoring.genomes) <> 1001 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Scoring tutorial requires the complete recorded cohort';
    END IF;
END
$check$;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.alignments CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.alignments AS
SELECT q.accession,
       bioseq.target_start(t.seq)::integer AS target_start,
       bioseq.target_end(t.seq)::integer AS target_end,
       bioseq.query_start(t.seq)::integer AS query_start,
       bioseq.query_end(t.seq)::integer AS query_end,
       bioseq.is_reverse(t.seq) AS is_reverse,
       bioseq.cigar(t.seq)::text AS cigar,
       bioseq.edit(t.seq) AS edits,
       bioseq.score(t.seq) AS score,
       bioseq.is_primary(t.seq) AS is_primary
FROM scoring.genomes t
JOIN scoring.genomes q ON mmsearch(t.seq, q.seq, aligner_options(
    kmer_size => 15, window_size => 10,
    max_gap => 200, min_chain_score => 40))
WHERE t.role = 'reference' AND q.role = 'sample';

-- Choose one forward primary alignment per genome. Any unexpected split,
-- reversed or uncovered sequence is visible in the quality report.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.best_alignment AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (accession) *
FROM scoring.alignments
WHERE is_primary AND NOT is_reverse
ORDER BY accession, score DESC, target_start, query_start;
SELECT count(*) AS aligned_samples,
       min(target_end - target_start) AS shortest_reference_span,
       max(target_end - target_start) AS longest_reference_span,
       min(edits) AS fewest_edits, max(edits) AS most_edits
FROM scoring.best_alignment;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cigar_runs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cigar_runs AS
WITH operations AS (
    SELECT a.*, r.ordinality AS run,
           r.parts[1]::integer AS span, r.parts[2] AS op
    FROM scoring.best_alignment a
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_matches(a.cigar, '([0-9]+)([MIDNSHP=X])', 'g')
        WITH ORDINALITY AS r(parts, ordinality)
)
SELECT accession, run, span, op,
       target_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','D','N'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS ref_start0,
       query_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','I'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS query_start0
FROM operations;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.projected_sequences CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.projected_sequences AS
WITH sequences AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT accession, seq::text AS bases FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample'
), blocks AS (
    SELECT r.accession, string_agg(
        CASE WHEN op IN ('M','=','X') THEN substr(g.bases,r.query_start0+1,r.span)
             WHEN op IN ('D','N') THEN repeat('-',r.span)
             ELSE '' END, '' ORDER BY run) AS aligned
    FROM scoring.cigar_runs r JOIN sequences g USING (accession)
    GROUP BY r.accession
)
SELECT a.accession,
       repeat('-',a.target_start) || b.aligned ||
       repeat('-', bioseq.len(g.seq)::integer-a.target_end) AS aligned
FROM scoring.best_alignment a JOIN blocks b USING (accession)
CROSS JOIN scoring.genomes g WHERE g.role = 'reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.reference_bases CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.reference_bases AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base
FROM scoring.genomes g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.seq::text,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
WHERE g.role='reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.site_counts AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base, count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.projected_sequences g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.aligned,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
GROUP BY p.pos,p.base;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.site_counts(position1,base);

SELECT base, sum(n) AS aligned_calls
FROM scoring.site_counts GROUP BY base ORDER BY base;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.nucleotide_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.nucleotide_pairs AS
SELECT a.base AS base_from,b.base AS base_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.base=b.base THEN a.n*(a.n-1)
                ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
FROM scoring.site_counts a JOIN scoring.site_counts b USING(position1)
JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND a.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND b.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
GROUP BY a.base,b.base;

-- Ordered pairs give a symmetric matrix and use e_ij = p_i * p_j.
-- Two orientations represent each unordered pair of different samples.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.nucleotide_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *, pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER () AS q
    FROM scoring.nucleotide_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT base_from AS base, sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY base_from
)
SELECT f.base_from, f.base_to, pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.base_from<>f.base_to THEN
           pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER (WHERE f.base_from<>f.base_to)
               OVER (PARTITION BY f.base_from),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.base=f.base_from
JOIN marginals b ON b.base=f.base_to;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.reference_spectrum AS
WITH tallies AS (
    SELECT r.base AS reference_base,s.base AS sample_base,sum(s.n)::bigint AS calls
    FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
    WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
    GROUP BY r.base,s.base
)
SELECT *, calls::numeric/sum(calls) OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base) AS fraction_of_calls,
       CASE WHEN reference_base<>sample_base THEN
         calls::numeric/nullif(sum(calls) FILTER(WHERE reference_base<>sample_base)
             OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM tallies;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.position_summary AS
SELECT s.position1,r.base AS reference_base,
       sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS called_samples,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='N'),0) AS unknown_n,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='-'),0) AS gaps,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base<>r.base),0) AS reference_differences,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS observed_bases
FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
GROUP BY s.position1,r.base;

SELECT base_from,base_to,pairs,round(score_half_bits,2) AS score,
       round(100*fraction_of_differences,2) AS difference_percent
FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix ORDER BY base_from,base_to;

    gene text PRIMARY KEY,start0 integer,end0 integer,strand text,reference_protein text
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.mitochondrial_code (codon text PRIMARY KEY,aa text);
TRUNCATE scoring.mitochondrial_code;
-- NCBI translation table 2; codon enumeration is T,C,A,G at each position.
INSERT INTO scoring.mitochondrial_code
SELECT a.base||b.base||c.base,
       substr('FFLLSSSSYY**CCWWLLLLPPPPHHQQRRRRIIMMTTTTNNKKSS**VVVVAAAADDEEGGGG',
              ((a.i-1)*16+(b.i-1)*4+c.i)::integer,1)
FROM unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY a(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY b(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY c(base,i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cds_quality AS
SELECT p.accession,c.gene,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scoring.cigar_runs r WHERE r.accession=p.accession
      AND ((r.op='I' AND r.ref_start0>c.start0 AND r.ref_start0<c.end0)
        OR (r.op IN ('D','N') AND r.ref_start0<c.end0 AND r.ref_start0+r.span>c.start0)))
      AS has_indel,
    a.target_start>c.start0 OR a.target_end<c.end0 AS incompletely_aligned
FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
JOIN scoring.best_alignment a ON a.accession=p.accession;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.codons CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.codons AS
WITH coding AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT p.accession,c.gene,c.reference_protein,
       CASE WHEN c.strand='+' THEN substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0)
       ELSE reverse(translate(substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0),'ACGT','TGCA')) END AS bases
    FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
    JOIN scoring.cds_quality q ON q.accession=p.accession AND q.gene=c.gene
    WHERE NOT q.has_indel AND NOT q.incompletely_aligned
)
SELECT accession,gene,i AS codon1,substr(bases,3*i-2,3) AS codon,
       substr(reference_protein,i,1) AS reference_aa
FROM coding CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1,length(reference_protein)) x(i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.amino_acids CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.amino_acids AS
SELECT c.accession,c.gene,c.codon1,c.codon,c.reference_aa,
       CASE WHEN c.codon1=1 AND c.codon IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')
              THEN 'M' ELSE t.aa END AS aa
FROM scoring.codons c LEFT JOIN scoring.mitochondrial_code t USING(codon);
-- SQL NULL represents an ambiguous/unmapped codon; '*' represents a stop.
-- N as an amino acid is asparagine and is retained.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_cds_quality AS
SELECT accession,gene,bool_or(coalesce(aa='*',false)) AS premature_stop,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon ~ '^[ACGT]{3}$' AND codon NOT IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')) AS invalid_start,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon !~ '^[ACGT]{3}$') AS ambiguous_start
FROM scoring.amino_acids GROUP BY accession,gene;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_site_counts AS
SELECT a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa,count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.amino_acids a JOIN scoring.protein_cds_quality q USING(accession,gene)
WHERE NOT q.premature_stop AND NOT q.invalid_start AND NOT q.ambiguous_start AND aa IS NOT NULL AND aa<>'*' GROUP BY a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.protein_site_counts(gene,codon1,aa);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_pairs AS
WITH observed AS (
    SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.aa=b.aa THEN a.n*(a.n-1) ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
    FROM scoring.protein_site_counts a JOIN scoring.protein_site_counts b USING(gene,codon1)
    GROUP BY a.aa,b.aa
), alphabet AS (SELECT unnest(string_to_array('A R N D C Q E G H I L K M F P S T W Y V',' ')) AS aa)
SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,coalesce(o.pairs,0)::bigint AS pairs
FROM alphabet a CROSS JOIN alphabet b
LEFT JOIN observed o ON o.aa_from=a.aa AND o.aa_to=b.aa;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.protein_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *,pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER() AS q FROM scoring.protein_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT aa_from AS aa,sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY aa_from
)
SELECT f.aa_from,f.aa_to,pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.aa_from<>f.aa_to THEN
         pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER(WHERE f.aa_from<>f.aa_to)
           OVER(PARTITION BY f.aa_from),0) END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.aa=f.aa_from JOIN marginals b ON b.aa=f.aa_to;

SELECT gene,count(*) AS sample_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE has_indel) AS indel_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE incompletely_aligned) AS incomplete_cds
FROM scoring.cds_quality GROUP BY gene ORDER BY gene;
SELECT count(*) AS codons,count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa IS NULL) AS ambiguous_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='*') AS stop_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='N') AS asparagine_codons
FROM scoring.amino_acids;
-- bioseq:visible
WITH observed AS (
    SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.aa=b.aa THEN a.n*(a.n-1) ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
    FROM scoring.protein_site_counts a JOIN scoring.protein_site_counts b USING(gene,codon1)
    GROUP BY a.aa,b.aa
), alphabet AS (SELECT unnest(string_to_array('A R N D C Q E G H I L K M F P S T W Y V',' ')) AS aa)
SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,coalesce(o.pairs,0)::bigint AS pairs
FROM alphabet a CROSS JOIN alphabet b
LEFT JOIN observed o ON o.aa_from=a.aa AND o.aa_to=b.aa
WHERE a.aa = 'L' ORDER BY b.aa;
-- bioseq:teardown
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS scoring CASCADE;
```
<!-- scoring:protein-pairs:end -->

Longer proteins contribute more columns because we pool the accepted codons across all 13 genes. Within each column, every retained sample has equal weight. The resulting cohort frequencies therefore reflect both the protein lengths and the number of callable samples at each position.

<!-- scoring:protein-matrix:start -->

```sql runnable id=scoring_protein_matrix timeout=60s
CREATE TABLE scoring.snapshot (
    header text, seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;
SELECT bioseq.load('scoring.snapshot', 'scoring_matrices_cohort.fasta');
INSERT INTO scoring.genomes
SELECT split_part(header, ' ', 1),
       CASE WHEN split_part(header, ' ', 1) = 'NC_012920.1'
            THEN 'reference' ELSE 'sample' END,
       seq
FROM scoring.snapshot;
DROP TABLE scoring.snapshot;
DO $check$
BEGIN
    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample') <> 1000
       OR (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'reference') <> 1
       OR (SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM scoring.genomes) <> 1001 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Scoring tutorial requires the complete recorded cohort';
    END IF;
END
$check$;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.alignments CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.alignments AS
SELECT q.accession,
       bioseq.target_start(t.seq)::integer AS target_start,
       bioseq.target_end(t.seq)::integer AS target_end,
       bioseq.query_start(t.seq)::integer AS query_start,
       bioseq.query_end(t.seq)::integer AS query_end,
       bioseq.is_reverse(t.seq) AS is_reverse,
       bioseq.cigar(t.seq)::text AS cigar,
       bioseq.edit(t.seq) AS edits,
       bioseq.score(t.seq) AS score,
       bioseq.is_primary(t.seq) AS is_primary
FROM scoring.genomes t
JOIN scoring.genomes q ON mmsearch(t.seq, q.seq, aligner_options(
    kmer_size => 15, window_size => 10,
    max_gap => 200, min_chain_score => 40))
WHERE t.role = 'reference' AND q.role = 'sample';

-- Choose one forward primary alignment per genome. Any unexpected split,
-- reversed or uncovered sequence is visible in the quality report.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.best_alignment AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (accession) *
FROM scoring.alignments
WHERE is_primary AND NOT is_reverse
ORDER BY accession, score DESC, target_start, query_start;
SELECT count(*) AS aligned_samples,
       min(target_end - target_start) AS shortest_reference_span,
       max(target_end - target_start) AS longest_reference_span,
       min(edits) AS fewest_edits, max(edits) AS most_edits
FROM scoring.best_alignment;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cigar_runs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cigar_runs AS
WITH operations AS (
    SELECT a.*, r.ordinality AS run,
           r.parts[1]::integer AS span, r.parts[2] AS op
    FROM scoring.best_alignment a
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_matches(a.cigar, '([0-9]+)([MIDNSHP=X])', 'g')
        WITH ORDINALITY AS r(parts, ordinality)
)
SELECT accession, run, span, op,
       target_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','D','N'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS ref_start0,
       query_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','I'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS query_start0
FROM operations;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.projected_sequences CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.projected_sequences AS
WITH sequences AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT accession, seq::text AS bases FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample'
), blocks AS (
    SELECT r.accession, string_agg(
        CASE WHEN op IN ('M','=','X') THEN substr(g.bases,r.query_start0+1,r.span)
             WHEN op IN ('D','N') THEN repeat('-',r.span)
             ELSE '' END, '' ORDER BY run) AS aligned
    FROM scoring.cigar_runs r JOIN sequences g USING (accession)
    GROUP BY r.accession
)
SELECT a.accession,
       repeat('-',a.target_start) || b.aligned ||
       repeat('-', bioseq.len(g.seq)::integer-a.target_end) AS aligned
FROM scoring.best_alignment a JOIN blocks b USING (accession)
CROSS JOIN scoring.genomes g WHERE g.role = 'reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.reference_bases CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.reference_bases AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base
FROM scoring.genomes g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.seq::text,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
WHERE g.role='reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.site_counts AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base, count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.projected_sequences g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.aligned,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
GROUP BY p.pos,p.base;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.site_counts(position1,base);

SELECT base, sum(n) AS aligned_calls
FROM scoring.site_counts GROUP BY base ORDER BY base;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.nucleotide_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.nucleotide_pairs AS
SELECT a.base AS base_from,b.base AS base_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.base=b.base THEN a.n*(a.n-1)
                ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
FROM scoring.site_counts a JOIN scoring.site_counts b USING(position1)
JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND a.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND b.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
GROUP BY a.base,b.base;

-- Ordered pairs give a symmetric matrix and use e_ij = p_i * p_j.
-- Two orientations represent each unordered pair of different samples.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.nucleotide_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *, pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER () AS q
    FROM scoring.nucleotide_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT base_from AS base, sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY base_from
)
SELECT f.base_from, f.base_to, pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.base_from<>f.base_to THEN
           pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER (WHERE f.base_from<>f.base_to)
               OVER (PARTITION BY f.base_from),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.base=f.base_from
JOIN marginals b ON b.base=f.base_to;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.reference_spectrum AS
WITH tallies AS (
    SELECT r.base AS reference_base,s.base AS sample_base,sum(s.n)::bigint AS calls
    FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
    WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
    GROUP BY r.base,s.base
)
SELECT *, calls::numeric/sum(calls) OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base) AS fraction_of_calls,
       CASE WHEN reference_base<>sample_base THEN
         calls::numeric/nullif(sum(calls) FILTER(WHERE reference_base<>sample_base)
             OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM tallies;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.position_summary AS
SELECT s.position1,r.base AS reference_base,
       sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS called_samples,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='N'),0) AS unknown_n,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='-'),0) AS gaps,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base<>r.base),0) AS reference_differences,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS observed_bases
FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
GROUP BY s.position1,r.base;

SELECT base_from,base_to,pairs,round(score_half_bits,2) AS score,
       round(100*fraction_of_differences,2) AS difference_percent
FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix ORDER BY base_from,base_to;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.cds (
    gene text PRIMARY KEY,start0 integer,end0 integer,strand text,reference_protein text
);
TRUNCATE scoring.cds;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.mitochondrial_code (codon text PRIMARY KEY,aa text);
TRUNCATE scoring.mitochondrial_code;
-- NCBI translation table 2; codon enumeration is T,C,A,G at each position.
INSERT INTO scoring.mitochondrial_code
SELECT a.base||b.base||c.base,
       substr('FFLLSSSSYY**CCWWLLLLPPPPHHQQRRRRIIMMTTTTNNKKSS**VVVVAAAADDEEGGGG',
              ((a.i-1)*16+(b.i-1)*4+c.i)::integer,1)
FROM unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY a(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY b(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY c(base,i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cds_quality AS
SELECT p.accession,c.gene,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scoring.cigar_runs r WHERE r.accession=p.accession
      AND ((r.op='I' AND r.ref_start0>c.start0 AND r.ref_start0<c.end0)
        OR (r.op IN ('D','N') AND r.ref_start0<c.end0 AND r.ref_start0+r.span>c.start0)))
      AS has_indel,
    a.target_start>c.start0 OR a.target_end<c.end0 AS incompletely_aligned
FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
JOIN scoring.best_alignment a ON a.accession=p.accession;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.codons CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.codons AS
WITH coding AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT p.accession,c.gene,c.reference_protein,
       CASE WHEN c.strand='+' THEN substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0)
       ELSE reverse(translate(substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0),'ACGT','TGCA')) END AS bases
    FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
    JOIN scoring.cds_quality q ON q.accession=p.accession AND q.gene=c.gene
    WHERE NOT q.has_indel AND NOT q.incompletely_aligned
)
SELECT accession,gene,i AS codon1,substr(bases,3*i-2,3) AS codon,
       substr(reference_protein,i,1) AS reference_aa
FROM coding CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1,length(reference_protein)) x(i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.amino_acids CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.amino_acids AS
SELECT c.accession,c.gene,c.codon1,c.codon,c.reference_aa,
       CASE WHEN c.codon1=1 AND c.codon IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')
              THEN 'M' ELSE t.aa END AS aa
FROM scoring.codons c LEFT JOIN scoring.mitochondrial_code t USING(codon);
-- SQL NULL represents an ambiguous/unmapped codon; '*' represents a stop.
-- N as an amino acid is asparagine and is retained.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_cds_quality AS
SELECT accession,gene,bool_or(coalesce(aa='*',false)) AS premature_stop,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon ~ '^[ACGT]{3}$' AND codon NOT IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')) AS invalid_start,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon !~ '^[ACGT]{3}$') AS ambiguous_start
FROM scoring.amino_acids GROUP BY accession,gene;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_site_counts AS
SELECT a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa,count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.amino_acids a JOIN scoring.protein_cds_quality q USING(accession,gene)
WHERE NOT q.premature_stop AND NOT q.invalid_start AND NOT q.ambiguous_start AND aa IS NOT NULL AND aa<>'*' GROUP BY a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.protein_site_counts(gene,codon1,aa);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_pairs AS
WITH observed AS (
    SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.aa=b.aa THEN a.n*(a.n-1) ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
    FROM scoring.protein_site_counts a JOIN scoring.protein_site_counts b USING(gene,codon1)
    GROUP BY a.aa,b.aa
), alphabet AS (SELECT unnest(string_to_array('A R N D C Q E G H I L K M F P S T W Y V',' ')) AS aa)
SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,coalesce(o.pairs,0)::bigint AS pairs
FROM alphabet a CROSS JOIN alphabet b
LEFT JOIN observed o ON o.aa_from=a.aa AND o.aa_to=b.aa;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.protein_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *,pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER() AS q FROM scoring.protein_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT aa_from AS aa,sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY aa_from
)
SELECT f.aa_from,f.aa_to,pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.aa_from<>f.aa_to THEN
         pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER(WHERE f.aa_from<>f.aa_to)
           OVER(PARTITION BY f.aa_from),0) END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.aa=f.aa_from JOIN marginals b ON b.aa=f.aa_to;

SELECT gene,count(*) AS sample_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE has_indel) AS indel_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE incompletely_aligned) AS incomplete_cds
FROM scoring.cds_quality GROUP BY gene ORDER BY gene;
SELECT count(*) AS codons,count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa IS NULL) AS ambiguous_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='*') AS stop_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='N') AS asparagine_codons
FROM scoring.amino_acids;
-- bioseq:visible
SELECT aa_from, aa_to, pairs,
       round(score_half_bits, 2) AS score_half_bits,
       round(100 * fraction_of_differences, 4) AS percent_of_differences
FROM scoring.protein_matrix
WHERE aa_from = 'L'
ORDER BY aa_to;
-- bioseq:teardown
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS scoring CASCADE;
```
<!-- scoring:protein-matrix:end -->

[![Twenty-by-twenty amino-acid log-odds matrix from corresponding mitochondrial coding positions.](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-scores.svg)](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-scores.svg)

The slashed cells mark pairs we never observed. For a zero observed frequency, the unsmoothed log odds is $-\infty$. The SQL leaves those scores empty rather than replacing them with an arbitrary finite penalty. Smoothing would require an explicit prior and its weight, especially for rare pairs.

All 13 genes retain coding regions from the cohort. The start-codon filter removes 14 sample/gene combinations: one ND5 region starts with GTA, and 13 other regions have an unresolved first codon. Among the retained regions, 1,540 ambiguous codons are excluded, leaving 3,784,719 callable amino-acid observations. Amino-acid N remains present in 163,715 of those observations.

There are 317 positions with more than one observed amino acid. Of the 400 ordered matrix cells, 284 have no observed pair, which is why much of this heatmap is slashed. A thousand closely related samples still provide limited evidence about many possible amino-acid exchanges.

This calculation uses BLOSUM's log-odds idea with our cohort's frequencies. Actual BLOSUM62 construction includes clustering at its identity threshold to control redundant sequences. These human mitochondrial proteins are so similar that applying that threshold would merge much of our cohort, leaving very little independent between-cluster evidence. Equal sample weights instead answer the question we asked here: which aligned residue pairs occur in these thousand records?

### Compare the differing amino-acid partners

The original BLOSUM62 joint probabilities are available in [NCBI's BLAST source](https://github.com/ncbi/ncbi-cxx-toolkit-public/blob/main/src/algo/blast/composition_adjustment/matrix_frequency_data.c). They retain the frequency information that is lost when scores are rounded to integers. The example bundle includes those reference tables and their source information.

For each amino acid $a$, we remove its identical partner from the denominator and normalize the remaining ordered joint frequencies:

$$
P(b\mid a,\ b\ne a)=\frac{Q_{ab}}{\sum_{c\ne a}Q_{ac}}.
$$

Apply that equation to both the cohort and BLOSUM62, and each row becomes a distribution over differing partners. For example, the L row asks how much of the leucine pairing with a different residue involves isoleucine, valine and the other amino acids.

```sql runnable id=scoring_protein_ratios timeout=60s
CREATE TABLE scoring.snapshot (
    header text, seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;
SELECT bioseq.load('scoring.snapshot', 'scoring_matrices_cohort.fasta');
INSERT INTO scoring.genomes
SELECT split_part(header, ' ', 1),
       CASE WHEN split_part(header, ' ', 1) = 'NC_012920.1'
            THEN 'reference' ELSE 'sample' END,
       seq
FROM scoring.snapshot;
DROP TABLE scoring.snapshot;
DO $check$
BEGIN
    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample') <> 1000
       OR (SELECT count(*) FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'reference') <> 1
       OR (SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM scoring.genomes) <> 1001 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Scoring tutorial requires the complete recorded cohort';
    END IF;
END
$check$;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.alignments CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.alignments AS
SELECT q.accession,
       bioseq.target_start(t.seq)::integer AS target_start,
       bioseq.target_end(t.seq)::integer AS target_end,
       bioseq.query_start(t.seq)::integer AS query_start,
       bioseq.query_end(t.seq)::integer AS query_end,
       bioseq.is_reverse(t.seq) AS is_reverse,
       bioseq.cigar(t.seq)::text AS cigar,
       bioseq.edit(t.seq) AS edits,
       bioseq.score(t.seq) AS score,
       bioseq.is_primary(t.seq) AS is_primary
FROM scoring.genomes t
JOIN scoring.genomes q ON mmsearch(t.seq, q.seq, aligner_options(
    kmer_size => 15, window_size => 10,
    max_gap => 200, min_chain_score => 40))
WHERE t.role = 'reference' AND q.role = 'sample';

-- Choose one forward primary alignment per genome. Any unexpected split,
-- reversed or uncovered sequence is visible in the quality report.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.best_alignment AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (accession) *
FROM scoring.alignments
WHERE is_primary AND NOT is_reverse
ORDER BY accession, score DESC, target_start, query_start;
SELECT count(*) AS aligned_samples,
       min(target_end - target_start) AS shortest_reference_span,
       max(target_end - target_start) AS longest_reference_span,
       min(edits) AS fewest_edits, max(edits) AS most_edits
FROM scoring.best_alignment;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cigar_runs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cigar_runs AS
WITH operations AS (
    SELECT a.*, r.ordinality AS run,
           r.parts[1]::integer AS span, r.parts[2] AS op
    FROM scoring.best_alignment a
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_matches(a.cigar, '([0-9]+)([MIDNSHP=X])', 'g')
        WITH ORDINALITY AS r(parts, ordinality)
)
SELECT accession, run, span, op,
       target_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','D','N'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS ref_start0,
       query_start + coalesce(sum(span) FILTER (WHERE op IN ('M','=','X','I'))
         OVER (PARTITION BY accession ORDER BY run ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),0)::integer AS query_start0
FROM operations;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.projected_sequences CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.projected_sequences AS
WITH sequences AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT accession, seq::text AS bases FROM scoring.genomes WHERE role = 'sample'
), blocks AS (
    SELECT r.accession, string_agg(
        CASE WHEN op IN ('M','=','X') THEN substr(g.bases,r.query_start0+1,r.span)
             WHEN op IN ('D','N') THEN repeat('-',r.span)
             ELSE '' END, '' ORDER BY run) AS aligned
    FROM scoring.cigar_runs r JOIN sequences g USING (accession)
    GROUP BY r.accession
)
SELECT a.accession,
       repeat('-',a.target_start) || b.aligned ||
       repeat('-', bioseq.len(g.seq)::integer-a.target_end) AS aligned
FROM scoring.best_alignment a JOIN blocks b USING (accession)
CROSS JOIN scoring.genomes g WHERE g.role = 'reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.reference_bases CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.reference_bases AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base
FROM scoring.genomes g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.seq::text,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
WHERE g.role='reference';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.site_counts AS
SELECT p.pos::integer AS position1, p.base, count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.projected_sequences g
CROSS JOIN LATERAL regexp_split_to_table(g.aligned,'')
  WITH ORDINALITY AS p(base,pos)
GROUP BY p.pos,p.base;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.site_counts(position1,base);

SELECT base, sum(n) AS aligned_calls
FROM scoring.site_counts GROUP BY base ORDER BY base;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.nucleotide_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.nucleotide_pairs AS
SELECT a.base AS base_from,b.base AS base_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.base=b.base THEN a.n*(a.n-1)
                ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
FROM scoring.site_counts a JOIN scoring.site_counts b USING(position1)
JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND a.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND b.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
GROUP BY a.base,b.base;

-- Ordered pairs give a symmetric matrix and use e_ij = p_i * p_j.
-- Two orientations represent each unordered pair of different samples.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.nucleotide_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *, pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER () AS q
    FROM scoring.nucleotide_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT base_from AS base, sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY base_from
)
SELECT f.base_from, f.base_to, pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.base_from<>f.base_to THEN
           pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER (WHERE f.base_from<>f.base_to)
               OVER (PARTITION BY f.base_from),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.base=f.base_from
JOIN marginals b ON b.base=f.base_to;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.reference_spectrum AS
WITH tallies AS (
    SELECT r.base AS reference_base,s.base AS sample_base,sum(s.n)::bigint AS calls
    FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
    WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')
    GROUP BY r.base,s.base
)
SELECT *, calls::numeric/sum(calls) OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base) AS fraction_of_calls,
       CASE WHEN reference_base<>sample_base THEN
         calls::numeric/nullif(sum(calls) FILTER(WHERE reference_base<>sample_base)
             OVER(PARTITION BY reference_base),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM tallies;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.position_summary AS
SELECT s.position1,r.base AS reference_base,
       sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS called_samples,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='N'),0) AS unknown_n,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE s.base='-'),0) AS gaps,
       coalesce(sum(s.n) FILTER(WHERE r.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base IN ('A','C','G','T') AND s.base<>r.base),0) AS reference_differences,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE s.base IN ('A','C','G','T')) AS observed_bases
FROM scoring.site_counts s JOIN scoring.reference_bases r USING(position1)
GROUP BY s.position1,r.base;

SELECT base_from,base_to,pairs,round(score_half_bits,2) AS score,
       round(100*fraction_of_differences,2) AS difference_percent
FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix ORDER BY base_from,base_to;

    gene text PRIMARY KEY,start0 integer,end0 integer,strand text,reference_protein text
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.mitochondrial_code (codon text PRIMARY KEY,aa text);
TRUNCATE scoring.mitochondrial_code;
-- NCBI translation table 2; codon enumeration is T,C,A,G at each position.
INSERT INTO scoring.mitochondrial_code
SELECT a.base||b.base||c.base,
       substr('FFLLSSSSYY**CCWWLLLLPPPPHHQQRRRRIIMMTTTTNNKKSS**VVVVAAAADDEEGGGG',
              ((a.i-1)*16+(b.i-1)*4+c.i)::integer,1)
FROM unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY a(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY b(base,i)
CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY['T','C','A','G']) WITH ORDINALITY c(base,i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.cds_quality AS
SELECT p.accession,c.gene,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scoring.cigar_runs r WHERE r.accession=p.accession
      AND ((r.op='I' AND r.ref_start0>c.start0 AND r.ref_start0<c.end0)
        OR (r.op IN ('D','N') AND r.ref_start0<c.end0 AND r.ref_start0+r.span>c.start0)))
      AS has_indel,
    a.target_start>c.start0 OR a.target_end<c.end0 AS incompletely_aligned
FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
JOIN scoring.best_alignment a ON a.accession=p.accession;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.codons CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.codons AS
WITH coding AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT p.accession,c.gene,c.reference_protein,
       CASE WHEN c.strand='+' THEN substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0)
       ELSE reverse(translate(substr(p.aligned,c.start0+1,c.end0-c.start0),'ACGT','TGCA')) END AS bases
    FROM scoring.projected_sequences p CROSS JOIN scoring.cds c
    JOIN scoring.cds_quality q ON q.accession=p.accession AND q.gene=c.gene
    WHERE NOT q.has_indel AND NOT q.incompletely_aligned
)
SELECT accession,gene,i AS codon1,substr(bases,3*i-2,3) AS codon,
       substr(reference_protein,i,1) AS reference_aa
FROM coding CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1,length(reference_protein)) x(i);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.amino_acids CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.amino_acids AS
SELECT c.accession,c.gene,c.codon1,c.codon,c.reference_aa,
       CASE WHEN c.codon1=1 AND c.codon IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')
              THEN 'M' ELSE t.aa END AS aa
FROM scoring.codons c LEFT JOIN scoring.mitochondrial_code t USING(codon);
-- SQL NULL represents an ambiguous/unmapped codon; '*' represents a stop.
-- N as an amino acid is asparagine and is retained.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_cds_quality CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_cds_quality AS
SELECT accession,gene,bool_or(coalesce(aa='*',false)) AS premature_stop,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon ~ '^[ACGT]{3}$' AND codon NOT IN ('ATT','ATC','ATA','ATG','GTG')) AS invalid_start,
       bool_or(codon1=1 AND codon !~ '^[ACGT]{3}$') AS ambiguous_start
FROM scoring.amino_acids GROUP BY accession,gene;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_site_counts CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_site_counts AS
SELECT a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa,count(*)::bigint AS n
FROM scoring.amino_acids a JOIN scoring.protein_cds_quality q USING(accession,gene)
WHERE NOT q.premature_stop AND NOT q.invalid_start AND NOT q.ambiguous_start AND aa IS NOT NULL AND aa<>'*' GROUP BY a.gene,a.codon1,a.aa;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON scoring.protein_site_counts(gene,codon1,aa);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scoring.protein_pairs CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE scoring.protein_pairs AS
WITH observed AS (
    SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,
       sum(CASE WHEN a.aa=b.aa THEN a.n*(a.n-1) ELSE a.n*b.n END)::bigint AS pairs
    FROM scoring.protein_site_counts a JOIN scoring.protein_site_counts b USING(gene,codon1)
    GROUP BY a.aa,b.aa
), alphabet AS (SELECT unnest(string_to_array('A R N D C Q E G H I L K M F P S T W Y V',' ')) AS aa)
SELECT a.aa AS aa_from,b.aa AS aa_to,coalesce(o.pairs,0)::bigint AS pairs
FROM alphabet a CROSS JOIN alphabet b
LEFT JOIN observed o ON o.aa_from=a.aa AND o.aa_to=b.aa;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.protein_matrix AS
WITH frequencies AS (
    SELECT *,pairs::numeric/sum(pairs) OVER() AS q FROM scoring.protein_pairs
), marginals AS (
    SELECT aa_from AS aa,sum(q) AS p FROM frequencies GROUP BY aa_from
)
SELECT f.aa_from,f.aa_to,pairs,q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       CASE WHEN q>0 THEN 2*log(2::numeric,q/(a.p*b.p)) END AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN f.aa_from<>f.aa_to THEN
         pairs::numeric/nullif(sum(pairs) FILTER(WHERE f.aa_from<>f.aa_to)
           OVER(PARTITION BY f.aa_from),0) END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM frequencies f JOIN marginals a ON a.aa=f.aa_from JOIN marginals b ON b.aa=f.aa_to;

SELECT gene,count(*) AS sample_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE has_indel) AS indel_cds,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE incompletely_aligned) AS incomplete_cds
FROM scoring.cds_quality GROUP BY gene ORDER BY gene;
SELECT count(*) AS codons,count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa IS NULL) AS ambiguous_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='*') AS stop_codons,
       count(*) FILTER(WHERE aa='N') AS asparagine_codons
FROM scoring.amino_acids;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.reference_joint (
    matrix text,aa_from text,aa_to text,q numeric,PRIMARY KEY(matrix,aa_from,aa_to)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.reference_scores (
    matrix text,aa_from text,aa_to text,score integer,units_per_bit integer,
    PRIMARY KEY(matrix,aa_from,aa_to)
);
TRUNCATE scoring.reference_joint,scoring.reference_scores;
CREATE TEMP TABLE incoming_joint(aa_from text,aa_to text,q numeric);
CREATE TEMP TABLE incoming_scores(aa_from text,aa_to text,score integer,units_per_bit integer);

INSERT INTO scoring.reference_scores SELECT 'PAM250',* FROM incoming_scores;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.reference_protein_matrix AS
WITH background AS (
    SELECT matrix,aa_from AS aa,sum(q) AS p
    FROM scoring.reference_joint GROUP BY matrix,aa_from
)
SELECT j.matrix,j.aa_from,j.aa_to,j.q,a.p*b.p AS expected,
       s.score,s.units_per_bit,2*log(2::numeric,j.q/(a.p*b.p)) AS score_half_bits,
       CASE WHEN j.aa_from<>j.aa_to THEN
           j.q/nullif(sum(j.q) FILTER(WHERE j.aa_from<>j.aa_to)
             OVER(PARTITION BY j.matrix,j.aa_from),0)
       END AS fraction_of_differences
FROM scoring.reference_joint j JOIN scoring.reference_scores s USING(matrix,aa_from,aa_to)
JOIN background a ON a.matrix=j.matrix AND a.aa=j.aa_from
JOIN background b ON b.matrix=j.matrix AND b.aa=j.aa_to;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scoring.matrix_entropy AS
SELECT 'Human mitochondrial DNA'::text AS matrix,
       sum(q*score_half_bits/2) AS bits_per_aligned_pair FROM scoring.nucleotide_matrix
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Human mitochondrial proteins',sum(q*score_half_bits/2) FROM scoring.protein_matrix
UNION ALL
SELECT matrix,sum(q*score_half_bits/2) FROM scoring.reference_protein_matrix GROUP BY matrix;
-- bioseq:visible
SELECT p.aa_from, p.aa_to,
       round(100 * p.fraction_of_differences, 4) AS cohort_percent,
       round(100 * b.fraction_of_differences, 4) AS blosum62_percent
FROM scoring.protein_matrix p
JOIN scoring.reference_protein_matrix b USING (aa_from, aa_to)
WHERE b.matrix = 'BLOSUM62'
  AND p.aa_from = 'L' AND p.aa_to <> 'L'
ORDER BY p.aa_to;
-- bioseq:teardown
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS scoring CASCADE;
```
<!-- scoring:protein-ratios:end -->

[![Conditional amino-acid partner frequencies calculated from NCBI's original BLOSUM62 probabilities.](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-partners-blosum62.svg)](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-partners-blosum62.svg)

[![Conditional amino-acid partner frequencies calculated from the mitochondrial cohort.](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-partners-cohort.svg)](/static/figures/blog/scoring-matrices/protein-partners-cohort.svg)

Both plots use the same alphabet and percentage scale. Open either matrix to inspect it at full size. Read across a row to compare the destinations. The underlying joint frequencies are symmetric, while these conditional rows can differ between directions because their denominators differ.

The leucine row gives a visible example. In the cohort, isoleucine accounts for 51.30% of differing partners of leucine and phenylalanine for 44.57%. The corresponding BLOSUM62 proportions are 18.43% and 8.77%. Alanine pairs with threonine in 88.61% of its differing cohort pairs, compared with 7.05% in BLOSUM62.

The average log odds is also different: 3.985 bits per aligned pair for the cohort proteins, compared with 0.698 bits for BLOSUM62. That larger value reflects how concentrated the cohort observations are on identical and a few differing pairs. It describes these frequencies, rather than measuring how well the matrix would perform in a search for distant proteins.

BLOSUM62 pools conserved blocks from many protein families at much greater divergence. Our matrix pools a single cohort's mitochondrial proteins, most of which sit in membrane complexes. The two collections give different evidence about amino-acid pairing. The observed differences are a reason to examine the source of a scoring matrix before applying it to a particular alignment task.

## Plot the SQL results with Python

At this point the CSV files contain the counts, marginal frequencies, log odds and conditional fractions. Python reads them and chooses how to display the axes and colors.

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install matplotlib==3.10.7
.venv/bin/python render_charts.py --results results --output figures
```

<!-- scoring:python-plots:start -->
```python
from pathlib import Path
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
import numpy as np
from render_charts import DNA, SCORE_MAP, figure, matrix, rows, save

records = rows(Path('results/nucleotide_matrix.csv'))
scores = matrix(records, DNA, 'base_from', 'base_to', 'score_half_bits')
fig, ax = figure(width=7, height=6)
edges = np.arange(len(DNA) + 1) - 0.5
image = ax.pcolormesh(edges, edges, scores, cmap=SCORE_MAP,
                      norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0), shading='flat')
ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xticks(range(4), DNA)
ax.set_yticks(range(4), DNA)
ax.set_xlabel('Partner nucleotide')
ax.set_ylabel('First nucleotide')
fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, label='Log-odds score (half bits)')
fig.tight_layout()
save(fig, Path('nucleotide-matrix.svg'),
     'Human mitochondrial nucleotide scores',
     'Log-odds scores from aligned nucleotide pairs in the 1,000-genome cohort.')
```
<!-- scoring:python-plots:end -->

The complete plotter writes the matrix heatmaps, nucleotide bars, quality plots and coordinate profiles shown here. Its SVG backgrounds are transparent, with separate text and accent colors for light and dark mode. Each plot keeps its numerical scale in its legend.

### From pairwise differences to a distance table

A substitution score adds evidence across an alignment. To describe how much two of these samples differ, we can also calculate their mismatch fraction directly:

$$
d_p=\frac{\text{differing aligned canonical bases}}{\text{aligned positions callable in both samples}}.
$$

The pipeline calculates this for eight selected accessions, using the projected alignment columns and removing N or gaps separately for each sample pair:

<!-- scoring:distances:start -->
```sql runnable id=scoring_distances timeout=60s
-- bioseq:setup
SET max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0;
SET bioseq.index.insert_maintenance.enabled = off;
SET bioseq.aligner.vulkan.enabled = off;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS scoring;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.genomes (
    accession text NOT NULL,
    role text NOT NULL,
    seq bioseq.seq('dna5', 64) NOT NULL
) USING bioseq;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scoring.samples (
    accession text PRIMARY KEY,isolate text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    organism text NOT NULL,bases integer NOT NULL,title text NOT NULL
);
TRUNCATE scoring.samples;
```
